# Verification analysis: dhcp-per-segment-gateway-ubuntu24

Job: `2026-09-06__11-26-15`

This report explains the verifier decisions recorded for this job. It interprets the saved evidence; it does not rerun the task or independently inspect the expired clusters.

## Task

> `node1` serves addresses on `lan-a` and `node2` serves addresses on `lan-b`.
> Have each router hand its own host an address from its own pool along with
> itself as that host's default route, so `node3` and `node4` each obtain
> their addressing from the router in front of them rather than from static
> configuration.

## Trial `dhcp-per-segment-gateway-ubuntu2__DEbVEAo`

**Verifier decision: Full Success.** All four material outcomes of the task are directly and coherently satisfied: node1 (VyOS) and node2 (OPNsense) each serve DHCP from their own pool on their own LAN with themselves as the default gateway, and node3/node4 are each shown obtaining addressing and a default route dynamically from their respective router rather than static configuration, confirmed by direct interface/route inspection and successful pings both before and after a full restart of all four nodes. The provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol is well-evidenced for all nodes with clear pre/post boot-identity pairs and recovered functional state, independently corroborated by the fixed lifecycle snapshots.

| Reward | Coverage | Functionality | Hygiene | Confidence | Commands |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.750 | 0.850 | 131/6 (+7 dropped) |

### Operational hygiene

The verifier assigned hygiene **0.750**. Most state-changing commands were either legitimate final configuration (VyOS eth2/Kea, OPNsense opt1/dnsmasq) or bounded, fully-reverted discovery probes: temporary IP addresses added to node3 enp8s0 (cmd-fd4f2f325c54491b) and node4 enp8s0 (cmd-be726415d4064964) for link mapping were deleted afterward (cmd-f5951d71d36843a4, cmd-120bd2f6aca24d70); a temporary probe address on node1 eth1 (cmd-7674a39509fb466f) and node2 vtnet1/vtnet2 (cmd-c801cf0b423f4c11, cmd-ed13e9b6357b4b65) used to rule out an unrelated router-to-router link were removed (cmd-11b3351b15b54f5c, cmd-97e68c7e08ef4d0f). Debug tcpdump processes and capture files on node1/node2/node4 were consistently killed and cleaned up (e.g. cmd-ddbca6602a98474b). One mutation is less clearly resolved: a Kea DHCPv4 subnet/service was enabled on node2 for vtnet2 (cmd-96836673cc1d4930) which failed to bind port 67 due to a conflict with the pre-existing dnsmasq DHCP service (visible in the kea log at cmd-dca479b2efbe4570); the executor's narrative states this was disabled in favor of dnsmasq, and the final sockstat check shows only dnsmasq bound to port 67 (cmd-1118eeaee2a94c71), but no explicit command disabling/removing the Kea subnet is visible in the trace, and FreeBSD's failed-service and package-health checks are unsupported in the lifecycle snapshots, so Kea's exact final enabled/disabled state on node2 cannot be independently confirmed from the captured evidence.

Hygiene evidence: `cmd-fd4f2f325c54491b`, `cmd-f5951d71d36843a4`, `cmd-be726415d4064964`, `cmd-120bd2f6aca24d70`, `cmd-7674a39509fb466f`, `cmd-11b3351b15b54f5c`, `cmd-c801cf0b423f4c11`, `cmd-ed13e9b6357b4b65`, `cmd-97e68c7e08ef4d0f`, `cmd-ddbca6602a98474b`, `cmd-96836673cc1d4930`, `cmd-dca479b2efbe4570`, `cmd-1118eeaee2a94c71`, `global:after_executor:node2:failed-services`, `global:after_executor:node2:package-health`

### Comments and limitations

- OPNsense (node2) lacks systemctl/package-manager-health support in the lifecycle snapshots, so it cannot be independently confirmed whether the Kea DHCPv4 service that was briefly enabled and failed to bind port 67 (cmd-96836673cc1d4930) was fully disabled/removed afterward, versus left in a non-functional but latent configuration state.
- Several OPNsense configuration mutations were applied via base64-encoded Python scripts whose exact contents are redacted in the evidence, limiting direct auditability of precisely what config.xml changes were made beyond what subsequent verification commands revealed.
- The public task instruction implies node3/node4 previously used static addressing, but the observed baseline network configuration for both (systemd-networkd DHCP=yes profile matching all 'en*' interfaces) was already DHCP-enabled prior to executor changes, so no removal of a static configuration was directly observed — the executor's action was effectively provisioning the missing DHCP server rather than migrating clients off static config.
- Operational hygiene was below a full pass (0.750); review the hygiene explanation above separately from functional success.
- Verifier confidence was 0.850; this is evidence confidence for this trial, not a repeatability estimate.
